definitions.gloss: new word; neologism; newly coined term
definitions.explanation: A word or expression that has been newly created or recently entered the language. Includes loanwords, slang, and technical terms that reflect changes in society and culture.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{新語|しんご}が{生|う}まれる。
examples.english: New words are born every year.

examples.japanese: {新語|しんご}・{流行語|りゅうこうご}{大賞|たいしょう}が{発表|はっぴょう}された。
examples.english: The New Words and Buzzwords of the Year Award was announced.

examples.japanese: インターネットの{普及|ふきゅう}とともに、{多|おお}くの{新語|しんご}が{日本語|にほんご}に{入|はい}ってきた。
examples.english: Along with the spread of the internet, many new words have entered Japanese.

notes:
Composed of {新|しん} (new) and {語|ご} (word, language). Refers to words that have recently appeared in the language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新語|しんご}・{流行語|りゅうこうご}{大賞|たいしょう}: New Words and Buzzwords of the Year Award
- {新語|しんご}が{生|う}まれる: new words are coined
- {新語|しんご}{辞典|じてん}: dictionary of new words
- {新語|しんご}を{作|つく}る: to coin a new word

CULTURAL NOTE:
The annual {新語|しんご}・{流行語|りゅうこうご}{大賞|たいしょう} (New Words and Buzzwords of the Year Award) is a popular year-end event in Japan, announced each December. It reflects social trends and cultural phenomena of that year.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {流行語|りゅうこうご}: buzzword — a word that becomes temporarily popular
- {新語|しんご}: neologism — a newly created or adopted word
- {造語|ぞうご}: coined word — emphasizes that the word was deliberately invented
- {廃語|はいご}: obsolete word — the opposite, a word that has fallen out of use
